description: Verify that DUT broadcasts an ARP Request when its cache lacks the destination's IP↔MAC entry — sending a packet to an unknown peer must trigger an ARP resolution attempt before the egress is sent (RFC 826 packet generation, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
The inverse of ARP_03: this case verifies that when DUT does NOT yet know an IP's MAC, it issues an ARP Request to resolve it before sending traffic. The cache is left empty (no learning stimulus is given); the test then forces DUT to send something to a new IP and watches for the resolution Request.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ Stimulates DUT to unicast-Nack back to HOST-1-IP. Subscribe-Nack is used because tc8-dut has no matching eventgroups, making it the smallest reliable trigger for unicast egress.
   ⇒ DUT needs HOST-1-IP's MAC; cache is empty so DUT must resolve.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode == 1 (Request)
      - sender_mac == DUT's interface MAC
      - target_ip  == HOST-1-IP
   The Ethernet broadcast destination (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff) is implicit per RFC 826 packet generation.

[Pass condition]
Within the observation window, DUT broadcasts an ARP Request whose opcode == 1 and sender_mac == DUT iface MAC.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_opcode — A frame matching the ARP Request shape was emitted but its opcode was not 1 (suspect malformed ARP)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit any ARP Request — it either silently dropped the egress or used some other resolution mechanism not allowed by the spec

verdicts.Pass: DUT broadcast an ARP Request with the expected opcode/sender — normal resolution
verdicts.Fail_opcode: An ARP-shaped frame was seen but its opcode was not 1 — malformed Request
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit any ARP Request within the window — resolution skipped or absent
